24: static wasm_val_t
25: pre_defined_val(wasm_valkind_t kind)
26: {
27:     if (kind == WASM_I32) {
28:         return wasm_val_t{ .kind = WASM_I32, .of = { .i32 = 2025 } };
29:     }
30:     else if (kind == WASM_I64) {
31:         return wasm_val_t{ .kind = WASM_I64, .of = { .i64 = 168 } };
32:     }
33:     else if (kind == WASM_F32) {
34:         return wasm_val_t{ .kind = WASM_F32, .of = { .f32 = 3.14159f } };
35:     }
36:     else if (kind == WASM_F64) {
37:         return wasm_val_t{ .kind = WASM_F64, .of = { .f64 = 2.71828 } };
38:     }
39:     else if (kind == WASM_EXTERNREF) {
40:         return wasm_val_t{ .kind = WASM_EXTERNREF,
41:                            .of = { .foreign = 0xabcddead } };
42:     }
43:     // because aft is_supported_val_kind() check, so we can safely return as
44:     // WASM_FUNCREF
45:     else {
46:         return wasm_val_t{ .kind = WASM_FUNCREF, .of = { .ref = nullptr } };

50: print_execution_args(const wasm_export_t &export_type,

85: static bool
86: execute_export_functions(wasm_module_t module, wasm_module_inst_t inst)
87: {
88:     int32_t export_count = wasm_runtime_get_export_count(module);
89: 
90:     for (int e_i = 0; e_i < export_count; e_i++) {
91:         wasm_export_t export_type = { 0 };
92:         wasm_runtime_get_export_type(module, e_i, &export_type);
93: 
94:         if (export_type.kind != WASM_IMPORT_EXPORT_KIND_FUNC) {
95:             continue;
96:         }
97: 
98:         wasm_function_inst_t func =
99:             wasm_runtime_lookup_function(inst, export_type.name);
100:         if (!func) {
101:             std::cout << "Failed to lookup function: " << export_type.name
102:                       << std::endl;
103:             continue;
104:         }
105: 
106:         wasm_func_type_t func_type = export_type.u.func_type;
107:         uint32_t param_count = wasm_func_type_get_param_count(func_type);
108: 
109:         /* build arguments */
110:         std::vector<wasm_val_t> args;
111:         for (unsigned p_i = 0; p_i < param_count; p_i++) {
112:             wasm_valkind_t param_type =
113:                 wasm_func_type_get_param_valkind(func_type, p_i);
114: 
115:             if (!is_supported_val_kind(param_type)) {
116:                 std::cout
117:                     << "Bypass execution because of unsupported value kind: "
118:                     << param_type << std::endl;
119:                 return true;
120:             }
121: 
122:             wasm_val_t arg = pre_defined_val(param_type);
123:             args.push_back(arg);
124:         }
125: 
126:         /* build results storage */
127:         uint32_t result_count = wasm_func_type_get_result_count(func_type);
128:         std::vector<wasm_val_t> results = std::vector<wasm_val_t>(result_count);
129: 
130:         print_execution_args(export_type, args, param_count);
131: 
132:         /* execute the function */
133:         wasm_exec_env_t exec_env = wasm_runtime_get_exec_env_singleton(inst);
134:         if (!exec_env) {
135:             std::cout << "Failed to get exec env" << std::endl;
136:             return false;
137:         }
138: 
139:         bool ret =
140:             wasm_runtime_call_wasm_a(exec_env, func, result_count,
141:                                      results.data(), param_count, args.data());
142:         if (!ret) {
143:             const char *exception = wasm_runtime_get_exception(inst);
144:             if (!exception) {
145:                 std::cout << "[EXECUTION] " << export_type.name
146:                           << "() failed. No exception info." << std::endl;
147:             }
148:             else {
149:                 std::cout << "[EXECUTION] " << export_type.name << "() failed. "
150:                           << exception << std::endl;
151:             }
152:         }
153: 
154:         wasm_runtime_clear_exception(inst);
155:     }
156: 
157:     return true;
158: }

161: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *Data, size_t Size)
162: {
163:     /* libfuzzer don't allow us to modify the given Data, so we copy the data
164:      * here */

167:     /* init runtime environment */

170:     char error_buf[128] = { 0 };
171:     wasm_module_t module =
172:         wasm_runtime_load((uint8_t *)myData.data(), Size, error_buf, 120);
173:     if (!module) {
174:         std::cout << "[LOADING] " << error_buf << std::endl;
175:         wasm_runtime_destroy();
176:         /* return SUCCESS because the failure has been handled */
177:         return 0;
178:     }

180:     wasm_module_inst_t inst = wasm_runtime_instantiate(
181:         module, 8 * 1024 * 1024, 16 * 1024 * 1024, error_buf, 120);
182:     if (!inst) {
183:         std::cout << "[INSTANTIATE] " << error_buf << std::endl;
184:         wasm_runtime_unload(module);

202: /* The custom mutator: */
203: #ifdef CUSTOM_MUTATOR
204: extern "C" size_t
205: LLVMFuzzerCustomMutator(uint8_t *Data, size_t Size, size_t MaxSize,
206:                         unsigned int Seed)
207: {
208:     if ((NULL != Data) && (Size > 10)) {
209:         int mutate_ret = -1;
210:         /* delete */
211:         if (access("./cur.wasm", 0) == 0) {
212:             remove("./cur.wasm");
213:         }
214: 
215:         /* 1.write data to cur.wasm */
216:         FILE *fwrite_fp = fopen("./cur.wasm", "wb");
217:         if (NULL == fwrite_fp) {
218:             printf("Faild to open cur.wasm file!\n");
219:             return 0;
220:         }
221:         fwrite(Data, sizeof(uint8_t), Size, fwrite_fp);
222:         fclose(fwrite_fp);
223:         fwrite_fp = NULL;
224: 
225:         /* 2.wasm-tools mutate modify cur.wasm */
226:         char cmd_tmp[150] = { 0 };
227: 
228:         /* clang-format off */
229:         const char *preserve_semantic = (Seed % 2) ? "--preserve-semantics" : "";
230:         sprintf(cmd_tmp, "wasm-tools mutate cur.wasm --seed %d -o modified.wasm %s > /dev/null 2>&1", Seed, preserve_semantic);
231:         /* clang-format on */
232:         mutate_ret = system(cmd_tmp);
233:         memset(cmd_tmp, 0, sizeof(cmd_tmp));
234: 
235:         if (mutate_ret != 0) {
236:             /* If source file not valid, use libfuzzer's own modifier */
237:             return LLVMFuzzerMutate(Data, Size, MaxSize);
238:         }
239: 
240:         /* 3.read modified file */
241:         int read_len = 0;
242:         int file_len = 0;
243:         int res = 0;
244:         uint8_t *buf = NULL;
245:         FILE *fread_fp = fopen("./modified.wasm", "rb");
246:         if (NULL == fread_fp) {
247:             printf("Faild to open modified.wasm file!\n");
248:             exit(0);
249:         }
250: 
251:         fseek(fread_fp, 0, SEEK_END); /* location to file end */
252:         file_len = ftell(fread_fp);   /* get file size */
253:         buf = (uint8_t *)malloc(file_len);
254: 
255:         if (NULL != buf) {
256:             fseek(fread_fp, 0, SEEK_SET); /* location to file start */
257:             read_len = fread(buf, 1, file_len, fread_fp);
258:             if ((read_len == file_len) && (read_len < MaxSize)) {
259:                 /* 4.fill Data buffer */
260:                 memcpy(Data, buf, read_len);
261:                 res = read_len;
262:             }
263:             else {
264:                 res = 0;
265:             }
266:         }
267:         else {
268:             res = 0;
269:         }
270: 
271:         memset(buf, 0, file_len);
272:         free(buf);
273:         fclose(fread_fp);
274:         fread_fp = NULL;
275: 
276:         return res;
277:     }
278:     else {
279:         if (access("./modified.wasm", 0) == 0) {
280:             remove("./modified.wasm");
281:         }
282:         memset(Data, 0, Size);
283:         Size = 0;
284:         return 0;
285:     }

# WAMR fuzz test framework

## install wasm-tools

```bash
1.git clone https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasm-tools
$ cd wasm-tools
2.This project can be installed and compiled from source with this Cargo command:
$ cargo install wasm-tools
3.Installation can be confirmed with:
$ wasm-tools --version
4.Subcommands can be explored with:
$ wasm-tools help
```

## Build

```bash
mkdir build && cd build
# Without custom mutator (libfuzzer modify the buffer randomly)
cmake ..
# TODO: TBC. `wasm-tools mutate` is not supported yet
# With custom mutator (wasm-tools mutate)
cmake .. -DCUSTOM_MUTATOR=1
make -j$(nproc)
```

## Manually generate wasm file in build

```bash
# wasm-tools smith generate some valid wasm file
# The generated wasm file is in corpus_dir under build
# N - Number of files to be generated
./smith_wasm.sh N 

# running
``` bash
cd build
./wasm-mutate-fuzz CORPUS_DIR
 
```

## Fuzzing Server

```shell
1. Installation Dependent Environment
$ cd server
$ pip install -r requirements.txt

2. Database Migration
$ python3 app/manager.py db init
$ python3 app/manager.py db migrate  
$ python3 app/manager.py db upgrade  

3. Change localhost to your machine's IP address
$ cd ../portal 
$ vim .env   # Change localhost to your machine's IP address  # http://<ip>:16667

4. Run Server and Portal
$ cd ..   # Switch to the original directory
If you want to customize the front-end deployment port:  # defaut 9999
    $ vim .env # Please change the portal_port to the port you want to use 

The server is deployed on port 16667 by default, If you want to change the server deployment port:
    $ vim .env # Please change the server_port to the port you want to use 
    $ vim portal/.env # Please change the VITE_SERVER_URL to the port you want to use  # http://ip:<port>


If your network needs to set up a proxy
    $ vim .env # Change proxy to your proxy address

$ docker-compose up --build -d
Wait for completion, Access the port set by env
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate seed wasm files exercising wasm_loader_prepare_bytecode paths."""
import os
import struct
import random
import sys

OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/gt/_work/corpus"

def leb(n):
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        b = n & 0x7F
        n >>= 7
        if n:
            out.append(b | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            return bytes(out)

def sleb(n):
    out = bytearray()
    more = True
    while more:
        b = n & 0x7F
        n >>= 7
        if (n == 0 and not (b & 0x40)) or (n == -1 and (b & 0x40)):
            more = False
        else:
            b |= 0x80
        out.append(b)
    return bytes(out)

class Builder:
    def __init__(self):
        self.types = b""     # type section body
        self.funcs = b""     # function section body
        self.codes = b""     # code section body
        self.type_count = 0
        self.func_type_idxs = []  # per function
        self.type_cache = {}

    def add_type(self, params, results):
        key = (tuple(params), tuple(results))
        if key in self.type_cache:
            return self.type_cache[key]
        idx = self.type_count
        self.type_count += 1
        body = bytearray()
        body.append(0x60)  # func
        body += leb(len(params))
        for p in params:
            body.append(p)
        body += leb(len(results))
        for r in results:
            body.append(r)
        self.types += bytes(body)
        self.type_cache[key] = idx
        return idx

    def add_func(self, type_idx):
        self.funcs += leb(type_idx)
        self.func_type_idxs.append(type_idx)

    def add_code(self, locals_decl, body):
        # locals_decl: list of (count, type)
        code = bytearray()
        lbody = bytearray()
        lbody += leb(len(locals_decl))
        for cnt, t in locals_decl:
            lbody += leb(cnt)
            lbody.append(t)
        code += leb(len(lbody) + len(body))
        code += lbody
        code += body
        code += b"\x0b"  # end
        self.codes += bytes(code)

    def section(self, sid, body):
        return bytes([sid]) + leb(len(body)) + body

    def finish(self, exports=None):
        out = bytearray(b"\x00\x61\x73\x6d\x01\x00\x00\x00")
        if self.types:
            out += self.section(1, self.types)
        if self.funcs:
            out += self.section(3, self.funcs)
        if self.codes:
            out += self.section(10, self.codes)
        return bytes(out)

I32, I64, F32, F64 = 0x7F, 0x7E, 0x7D, 0x7C

def const_i32(v):
    return bytes([0x41]) + sleb(v)

def const_i64(v):
    return bytes([0x42]) + sleb(v)

def const_f32(v):
    return bytes([0x43]) + struct.pack("<f", v)

def const_f64(v):
    return bytes([0x44]) + struct.pack("<d", v)

def local_get(i):
    return bytes([0x20]) + leb(i)

def local_set(i):
    return bytes([0x21]) + leb(i)

def local_tee(i):
    return bytes([0x22]) + leb(i)

def block_ty(t):
    return bytes([0x02]) + bytes([t])

def block_ty_idx(idx):
    return bytes([0x02]) + leb(idx)

def write(fname, data):
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, fname), "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)

os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

# 1. Simple function with locals and set/tee
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray(const_i32(1))
body += local_set(0)  # will be checked against stack types -> invalid, but loader ok?
body += const_i32(2)
body += local_tee(0)
b.add_code([(2, I32)], bytes(body))
write("seed_simple.wasm", b.finish())

# 2. Many locals, i64 ops
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I64])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
body += const_i64(0x1122334455667788)
body += const_i64(0x8877665544332211)
body += bytes([0x7c])  # i64.add
body += local_tee(0)
body += local_get(1)
body += bytes([0x7c])
b.add_code([(8, I64), (8, I32)], bytes(body))
write("seed_i64.wasm", b.finish())

# 3. Nested blocks with params
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
body += const_i32(5)
body += block_ty(I32)  # block (result i32)
body += local_get(0)
body += local_set(0)
body += const_i32(1)
body += bytes([0x0b])  # end
body += bytes([0x6a])  # i32.add
b.add_code([(3, I32)], bytes(body))
write("seed_block.wasm", b.finish())

# 4. if/else with locals
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([I32], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
body += local_get(0)
body += block_ty(I32)
body += local_get(0)
body += local_tee(1)
body += const_i32(7)
body += bytes([0x0b])
body += bytes([0x0b])
b.add_code([(4, I32), (2, I64)], bytes(body))
write("seed_if.wasm", b.finish())

# 5. loop + br
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
body += const_i32(0)
body += bytes([0x03]) + bytes([0x40])  # loop
body += const_i32(1)
body += bytes([0x6a])
body += local_tee(0)
body += bytes([0x0c]) + bytes([0x00])  # br 0
body += bytes([0x0b])
b.add_code([(1, I32)], bytes(body))
write("seed_loop.wasm", b.finish())

# 6. select i64
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I64])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
body += const_i64(1)
body += const_i64(2)
body += const_i32(1)
body += bytes([0x1b])  # select
body += local_tee(0)
b.add_code([(1, I64)], bytes(body))
write("seed_select_i64.wasm", b.finish())

# 7. big function: many locals and many set/get
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
for i in range(50):
    body += const_i32(i)
    body += local_set(i)
    body += local_get(i)
body += const_i32(0)
b.add_code([(60, I32)], bytes(body))
write("seed_big.wasm", b.finish())

# 8. select with f64 and typed select
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [F64])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
body += const_f64(1.5)
body += const_f64(2.5)
body += const_i32(1)
body += bytes([0x1b])  # select
b.add_code([], bytes(body))
write("seed_select_f64.wasm", b.finish())

# 9. typed select
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
body += const_i32(1)
body += const_i32(2)
body += const_i32(1)
body += bytes([0x1c]) + bytes([0x01]) + bytes([I32])  # select t
b.add_code([], bytes(body))
write("seed_select_t.wasm", b.finish())

# 10. block with func-type index as blocktype, params
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([I32, I32], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
bt = b.add_type([I32], [I32])
body = bytearray()
body += const_i32(3)
body += bytes([0x02]) + leb(bt)   # block (type idx with param)
body += local_get(0)
body += bytes([0x6a])
body += bytes([0x0b])
b.add_code([], bytes(body))
write("seed_blocktype_idx.wasm", b.finish())

# 11. deep nesting
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
for d in range(30):
    body += const_i32(d)
    body += bytes([0x02]) + bytes([0x40])
for d in range(30):
    body += bytes([0x0b])
body += const_i32(0)
b.add_code([(1, I32)], bytes(body))
write("seed_deep.wasm", b.finish())

# 12. locals referenced on stack across block boundary (preserve path)
b = Builder()
t = b.add_type([], [I32])
b.add_func(t)
body = bytearray()
# push 20 locals onto stack, then open a block -> preserve locals
for i in range(20):
    body += local_get(i)
body += bytes([0x02]) + bytes([0x40])
body += const_i32(1)
body += bytes([0x6a])   # add (i32)
body += bytes([0x1a])   # drop
body += bytes([0x0b])
body += const_i32(0)
b.add_code([(30, I32)], bytes(body))
write("seed_preserve.wasm", b.finish())

# 13. random-ish blob seeds (may be malformed, fine for mutation)
random.seed(1234)
for i in range(20):
    n = random.randint(64, 512)
    data = bytearray(b"\x00\x61\x73\x6d\x01\x00\x00\x00")
    data += bytes(random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))
    write(f"seed_rand_{i}.wasm", bytes(data))

print("seeds written to", OUT)
